blocks.value: Small as it is, every line is doing something. Working outward:

**`FirstJavaProgram` is a class name.** A **class** is the basic unit of a Java program: all Java code is grouped into a class. The definition starts with an **access modifier** (here, `public`), which specifies the accessibility of the class, followed by the keyword `class`.
**Braces mark boundaries.** Every class definition is enclosed in a pair of curly brackets, `{` and `}`. They mark where the class begins and ends.
**`main` is where execution starts.** The main method is a special method and is the entry point of program execution. A Java class can have only one `main` method.
**The line inside is a statement.** A **statement** is an action the program has to perform. Note the semicolon. Java requires one at the end of every statement.

blocks.value: A **literal string** is a series of characters that appear exactly as entered, written between double quotation marks. **Arguments** are information passed to a method so it can perform its task.
`println` prints and moves to the next line. `print` prints without the newline. You will use both.
